title: Every NWS future this observatory has ever called overdue was never overdue -- is_overdue compared window.to and now_iso by truncating both to their first 19 characters, which silently discards NWS's real UTC offset while GDACS's naive-UTC strings pass through unaffected
statement: practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's is_overdue (pre-fix, lines 36-41) read `to[:19] < now_iso[:19]` -- a lexical comparison of the first 19 characters of two ISO 8601 strings. GDACS's own window.to values are naive datetimes with no offset (e.g. foreknown/registry.json futures['gdacs-dr-1017863'].window.to == '2026-03-30T00:00:00', already UTC in this observatory's preserved bytes), so truncating to 19 characters and comparing against now_iso (always `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`, e.g. '2026-08-26T06:04:18+00:00' before its own +00:00 suffix) works by coincidence: both operands are UTC clock time once the offset suffix is dropped. NWS's CAP feed does not share that property -- practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py's nws_futures carries the alert's own local offset straight through (e.g. futures['nws-kmlb-maw-0267-26'].window.to == '2026-08-26T02:30:00-04:00', notarized tonight at announced_at '2026-08-26T06:04:14+00:00'). Truncating both to 19 characters and comparing lexically compares '2026-08-26T02:30:00' against '2026-08-26T06:04:14' as though they were the same clock -- '02:30:00' reads as already past -- when the window.to is actually 2026-08-26T06:30:00 UTC, 26 minutes after the run that just notarized it. is_overdue and the overdue_kind classification built on it (the machine's own sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift, promoted 2026-08-08) called this future cold_start_overdue on the very night it was first seen, before its announced window had even closed. Checked every NWS future this observatory has ever flagged overdue, using each night's own foreknown-notary-run timestamp from autonomy/log.jsonl as now_iso and each future's committed window.to from foreknown/registry.json (none of the 13 had a window REVISED event since notarization, so the committed value is the value in effect that night): 2026-08-23 (6: nws-kchs-maw-0108-26, nws-kmso-fww-0009-26, nws-kotx-fww-0022-26, nws-kpub-svw-0281-26, nws-krlx-faw-0106-26, nws-krnk-ffw-0035-26), 2026-08-24 (4: nws-kbuf-maw-0103-26, nws-kmhx-maw-0346-26, nws-ktwc-ffw-0151-26, nws-ktwc-ffw-0152-26), 2026-08-25 (2: nws-kabr-faw-0022-26, nws-kslc-ffw-0086-26), 2026-08-26 (1: nws-kmlb-maw-0267-26). All 13, on every night, recompute as not overdue once window.to and now_iso are both converted to real UTC instants before comparing. Zero true positives, zero exceptions, since NWS was audited into this observatory 2026-08-22 (foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-22/run.json's nws_overdue list is empty -- NWS's own first night). The shape is systematic, not incidental: every continental US NWS office reports a negative UTC offset, so truncated-string comparison always makes an NWS window.to read earlier than its true UTC instant by exactly the offset's magnitude, which is large enough (4 to 7 hours for the offices seen so far) to manufacture a false cold-start-overdue reading whenever a run happens to fall within that many hours of a genuine window close in local-clock digits. GDACS is unaffected because its own preserved bytes never carry an offset to begin with. Repaired tonight: added _as_utc (practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py, new lines 36-48), parsing each timestamp and treating an offset-less value as UTC before comparing, and rewired is_overdue and overdue_kind's cold-start/drift split to compare the resulting aware datetimes instead of truncated strings. A regression test (practice/tests/test_foreknown.py, test_overdue_compares_a_real_offset_not_a_truncated_string) reproduces nws-kmlb-maw-0267-26's exact figures -- not overdue at its own announced_at, genuinely drift_overdue 40 minutes past its true UTC close -- and the full suite (154 tests) passes. Not retroactive: foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-23 through 2026-08-26/run.json stay committed as written (I3); the 13 false positives are preserved evidence of the bug the fix now prevents from recurring, not corrected in place.
method: Noticed a single NWS future (nws-kmlb-maw-0267-26) in tonight's foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-26/run.json overdue_cold_start list on the same night it was notarized, which is the exact shape sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift's own docstring says should not happen for a genuine cold start (a warning whose window closed before the observatory ever saw it) -- this one was seen 26 minutes before its own announced close. Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's is_overdue and overdue_kind and found the `[:19]` truncated string comparison; converted foreknown/registry.json futures['nws-kmlb-maw-0267-26'].window.to and .announced_at to real UTC instants with python3's datetime.fromisoformat to confirm the true relationship (window closes after, not before, notarization). Generalised the check across every prior NWS overdue entry: for each night 2026-08-22 through 2026-08-26, read foreknown/snapshots/<date>/run.json's overdue list for nws- prefixed ids, cross-referenced each future's history in foreknown/registry.json for a window REVISED event (none found), took each night's own foreknown-notary-run timestamp from autonomy/log.jsonl as the now_iso the buggy code would have used, and recomputed is_overdue with a corrected UTC-aware comparison -- all 13 flip from overdue to not-overdue. Implemented the fix, wrote a regression test reproducing tonight's own figures, and ran the full suite (python3 -m pytest, from practice/) to confirm 154 pass (153 pre-existing plus the new one).
worth_watching_because: This is a case the observatory's own falsification and design language did not anticipate: sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift (foreknown/proposals/sensor-cold-start-overdue-drift.json, PROMOTED) was written and reviewed entirely against GDACS data, whose window fields happen to already be UTC; adding a second source with genuinely offset-carrying timestamps (NWS, audited 2026-08-22) silently broke an invariant the promoted sensor's correctness depended on without anyone -- human or machine -- re-examining it, because nothing about adding NWS touched the sensor's own file or its falsification clause. The failure mode is the same shape sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot and sensor-primary-iso3-gap both describe for GDACS-specific fields silently not applying to a second source, except here the miscount ran the other way: not a field the code fails to read, but a field format the code reads wrong for one source while reading it right for another, with no error, no failed test, and no autonomy/log.jsonl entry -- 13 confident false positives committed as fact across four consecutive nights before tonight. Worth a human's attention because it argues for auditing every function that compares or classifies raw source timestamps (not just is_overdue) whenever a new source is added, rather than assuming a check proven correct against one source's byte format stays correct against a second's.
left_alone: Not touching the three PROPOSED sensors (lead-time-pathway-idle, registry-stall, source-reconfirmation-blind-spot) -- lead-time-pathway-idle now has 4 of the 10 FORECAST-kind resolutions its test_rule waits for (foreknown/resolutions/nhc-al032026.json, nhc-cp022026.json, nhc-ep082026.json, nhc-ep102026.json, all NO_ALERT_MATCH; two FORECAST futures, nhc-cp012026 and nhc-ep092026, remain OPEN), still short of the threshold; the other two both carry open reviews asking for a firing-rule redesign, not more nights of the same data. Not auditing every other timestamp comparison in the codebase for the same offset-naive shape beyond is_overdue/overdue_kind -- grepped practice/src/practice/foreknown/*.py for `[:19]` and `[:10]` truncation and confirmed the remaining uses (history event dates in futures.py's drought-window series, resolve.py's cold_start day comparison) only ever compare this observatory's own utc_now()-stamped timestamps against each other, never against a raw source field, so they do not share this bug -- but a fuller audit of every raw source-timestamp read across sources.py and reaction.py is a larger task than one night's evidence settles, and is named here rather than attempted. Not writing a memoryhole/verdicts file -- the newest reading, memoryhole/readings/2026-08-24.json, still carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 20 entries and no newer reading exists yet. Not correcting foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-23 through 2026-08-26/run.json's committed overdue/overdue_cold_start lists in place -- they are preserved evidence of the bug (I3), not a live view; the fix takes effect from tonight's already-written run forward, the same reasoning foreknown/reaction/iso3-fips.json's 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-24 revisions both gave for not applying a correction retroactively.
